facts.claim: The venue describes all entries as accessible and says every restroom has accessible stalls. An elevator is near the first-floor entrance.
quote: All entries are accessible.
All restrooms have accessible stalls.
The elevator is on the first floor near the entrance.

facts.claim: Accessible parking is in the attached lower garage, with elevators to the main entry. ADA seating is sold through AXS.
quote: ADA parking is available in the lower attached parking garage operated by ABM Parking. Follow signage to the elevators for access to the main entry.
ADA seating is available through AXS.com

facts.claim: The venue requests at least two weeks' notice for a sign-language interpreter; late requests are considered when possible.
quote: We kindly ask that you submit your request at least two weeks prior to the concert date.
While we will do our best to accommodate late requests, advance notice is greatly appreciated.

facts.claim: Indoor ADA viewing is on the upper bar level, house right of the position the source labels FOH, and in Level 2 sections H and L. Outdoor ADA viewing is in the house-right area marked ADA and section F. For access questions, call 859-900-2294.
quote: Inside: Upper bar level house right of FOH and Level 2 sections H & L. Outside: House right area marked ADA & section F.
MegaCorp Pavilion can be reached at 859-900-2294

facts.claim: For general-admission shows, Guest Services staff can help with accessible seating on arrival.
quote: If you require ADA accessible seating for a general admission show, a member of our Guest Services staff can help accommodate your needs when you arrive.

facts.claim: Almost all shows are general-admission standing room only, and almost all have no re-entry.
quote: Almost all of our shows are general admission standing room only, which means that there is no assigned seating, if there's seating at all.
Almost all of our events have a "no re-entry" policy, which means once you enter, you cannot leave and re-enter.

facts.claim: Chairs, strollers, coolers, umbrellas and car seats are prohibited, as are non-service animals and prescriptions without a label.
quote: we do not allow the following items:
Coolers, chairs, umbrellas, strollers, car seats
Non-service animals
Unlabeled prescriptions

facts.claim: Indoor shows are non-smoking.
quote: Indoor shows are non-smoking.

facts.claim: For specific access arrangements, the venue asks guests to contact it reasonably in advance so it can make every effort to accommodate requests; this is not a guarantee of a particular arrangement.
quote: If you or a member of your party require ADA accommodations, we ask that you contact the venue reasonably in advance of the event you are attending, so we can make every effort to accommodate specific requests.

facts.claim: Send sign-language interpreter requests to Jemoore@promowestlive.com. The venue asks for at least two weeks before the concert and says it will do its best with later requests.
quote: To request a sign language interpreter, please email us at: Jemoore@promowestlive.com.
We kindly ask that you submit your request at least two weeks prior to the concert date.
While we will do our best to accommodate late requests, advance notice is greatly appreciated.

facts.claim: For access inquiries, the venue lists Feedback@promowestlive.com; guests may also look for a venue representative on arrival.
quote: For any ADA inquiry, please email us at: Feedback@promowestlive.com. You may also look for a venue representative when you arrive.

facts.claim: The box office is cashless and accepts major credit cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay.
quote: Please note our box office is cashless. All major credit cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay are accepted.

facts.claim: The ticket time is the door-opening time. Live music usually starts about an hour later, but this can change; the venue says bands decide set times.
quote: The time listed on your ticket is the time that the doors will open for the show. Live music will usually start about an hour after the doors open, but that's always subject to change. Also, we don't usually know the set times, that's up to the bands to decide.

facts.claim: The published bag policy allows clear plastic, vinyl or PVC totes up to 14 by 14 inches and small bags up to 5 by 8 by 1 inches; backpacks are not permitted. The page does not describe an exception for medical supplies, so confirm your arrangements before arrival.
quote: Clear Totes Plastic, vinyl, or PVC and does not exceed 14" x 14"
Small Bags Approximately the size of a hand with or without a handle or strap. No larger than 5" x 8" x 1"
Backpacks Are not permitted in any PromoWest venue

facts.claim: For box-office visits, the venue identifies a 15-minute parking zone on 3rd Street just outside the garage, with an elevator or steps up one floor. This is box-office arrival advice, not confirmation of event parking or the complete wheelchair route.
quote: To access the box office, fans can park in the 15 minute zone located on 3rd street just outside the parking garage and take elevator or steps up one floor.

facts.claim: The directions page lists box-office hours Tuesday–Friday 11 a.m.–3 p.m., and 3 p.m. opening on Saturday or Sunday event days; other weekends are closed. Major holidays are excluded, so confirm before a special trip.
quote: Box Office Hours Tuesday-Friday: 11am-3pm * Closed on Saturday and Sunday except for event days, open at 3pm * * Excluding major holidays.

address_quote: MegaCorp Pavilion 101 W 4th Street Newport, KY 41071

facts.claim: Great Parks’ dated alert places Shaker Trace Inner and Outer Loop paving on November 2–20, 2026. It describes base repairs where needed and a new 2-inch asphalt overlay, with temporary section closures, other sections kept open when possible and detour signs at intersections, road crossings and access points. Confirm current closures; the notice does not establish that work is finished.
quote: Shaker Trace Loop Trail Paving Project Start: October 29, 2026 End: November 20, 2026 Construction Miami Whitewater Forest
From November 2 - 20, contractors will be paving the Shaker Trace Trail Inner & Outer Loop at Miami Whitewater Forest.
Work includes repairing deteriorated subgrade and stone base where needed and installing a new 2-inch asphalt surface overlay along the trail.
Sections of the trail will be temporarily closed during repairs and paving. Work will be phased to allow other sections to remain open for visitor use whenever possible.
Detour and informational signage will be placed at trail intersections, road crossings, and trail access points.

facts.claim: A separate Great Parks alert, dated November 11, 2026–February 12, 2027, warns of possible intermittent Shaker Trace Loop closures for the golf-course irrigation project. Crews are to be on site for safety; this notice is separate from the November paving work.
quote: Shaker Trace Loop Closures Start: November 11, 2026 End: February 12, 2027 Construction Miami Whitewater Forest

Due to the Miami Whitewater Forest Golf Course Irrigation project, there may be intermittent closures to the Shaker Trace Loop trail. Crews will be onsite to ensure safety for both work crews and trail users.

facts.claim: Great Parks lists an accessible playground and a Zero G-Chair swing.
quote: Universally accessible playgrounds are located at: Francis RecreAcres Sharon Woods Winton Woods - Harper Meadows
Visitors can now use a Zero G-Chair Swing at Winton Woods, Sharon Woods, Lake Isabella, Woodland Mound, Miami Whitewater Forest, Shawnee Lookout and Embshoff Woods.

facts.claim: Great Parks says it will make every effort to provide reasonable accommodations for special events and educational programs with two weeks' advance notice. Contact Guest Relations at 513-521-7275 (Voice/TDD).
quote: Great Parks will make every effort, with two weeks advance notice, to provide reasonable accommodations so that people with disabilities may participate in special events and educational programs .
People with disabilities needing special accommodations for the accessibility of programs should contact Guest Relations at 513-521-7275, Voice/TDD.

facts.claim: Great Parks says Sharon Lake is being lowered from October 27 for harbor work and will stay lowered until spring 2027. Boat access is restricted while the water is down, and the harbor snack bar is closed during the project.
quote: Contractors will start lowering Sharon Lake on Tuesday, October 27. The lake will remain lowered until Spring 2027.
Boat access to the lake will be restricted while the water is down.
The Snack Bar at Sharon Woods Harbor will be closed during the Harbor Revitalization project .

facts.claim: The 0.6-mile Island Grove Trail is rated easy but labeled Not Accessible.
quote: 0.6 Miles Easy Shared-Use Trail Not Accessible

facts.claim: The 0.7-mile Lone Oak Trail is rated easy but labeled Not Accessible.
quote: 0.7 Miles Easy Shared-Use Trail Not Accessible

facts.claim: The 1.3-mile Buckeye Falls Trail is rated easy/moderate and labeled Not Accessible.
quote: 1.3 Mile Easy/Moderate Shared-Use Trail Not Accessible

facts.claim: Great Parks lists the harbor parking, restrooms, boathouse and playground as closed from October 2026 through completion of the harbor project.
quote: The following are closed from October 2026 through the project's completion: Harbor area (parking, restrooms, boathouse and playground)

facts.claim: The park phone is 513-563-4513.
During harbor construction, Great Parks directs visitors to the U.S. 42/Lebanon Road entrance, which remains open and connects to Buckeye Falls Drive.
quote: The Sharon Woods entrance from U.S. 42/Lebanon Road will remain open, and guests can use this entrance to connect to Buckeye Falls Drive, which leads all the way to Sharon Woods Golf Course.

facts.claim: The project page gives conflicting dates for the East Kemper Road entrance: its closure list says October 2026–May 2027, but its FAQ says until the harbor reopens. Confirm the entrance before travel; the harbor reopening is tentatively spring 2028.
quote: Entry drive from Kemper Road (Highbanks): October 2026-May 2027
Construction work will require Great Parks to close the Sharon Woods entrance from East Kemper Road until the harbor reopens.
Spring 2028 Harbor area reopens Timeline is an estimate based on the current project status and is subject to change.

facts.claim: The harbor project closes about 0.3 miles of Sharon Lake Trail from October 2026 through project completion, and about 0.1 miles of Buckeye Falls Trail near the harbor until the project finishes.
quote: Because the Sharon Lake Trail passes through the harbor, reconstruction of the harbor requires Great Parks to close a small section of the trail (approximately 0.3 miles) from October 2026 through the project's completion.
A short section of Buckeye Falls Trail (approximately 0.1 miles) near the harbor will also be closed until the project is finished.

facts.claim: The harbor-project FAQ says boating is not permitted until summer 2027, when the temporary boathouse at Lakeside Lodge on the east side of Sharon Lake is due to reopen. This is a planned reopening, not confirmation that boats are available now.
quote: Boating will not be permitted until summer 2027. Great Parks will reopen the temporary boathouse at Sharon Woods' Lakeside Lodge on the east side of Sharon Lake in summer 2027.

facts.claim: Great Parks requires a valid Motor Vehicle Permit for vehicle entry to its parks and conservation areas; its stated exceptions are Otto Armleder Memorial Park and Fernbank Park.
quote: A valid Motor Vehicle Permit (MVP) is required for vehicle entry at Great Parks’ parks and conservation areas across Hamilton County.
Otto Armleder Memorial Park and Fernbank Park are co-managed by Great Parks, the Cincinnati Park Board, and the Cincinnati Recreation Commission and do not require a Motor Vehicle Permit.

facts.claim: Sharon Center lists restrooms and parking. Its posted September 8–December 31, 2026 hours are daily 10 a.m.–5 p.m., with closures for Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas, New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day. Restroom layout and changing equipment are not described.
quote: Amenities Parking Playground Restrooms
2026 Hours
Sept. 8-Dec. 31 Daily 10 a.m.–5 p.m.
Closed Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas, New Year's Eve & New Year's Day

facts.claim: The Gorge Trail page lists a 0.6-mile nature trail rated Easy/Moderate, with parking and restrooms, open from dawn to dusk. It does not describe gradients, surface firmness, restroom layout or changing equipment; the rating is not a wheelchair-access statement.
quote: Amenities 0.6 miles Easy/Moderate Nature Trail Restrooms Parking Open daily from dawn until dusk

facts.claim: The garage under the square has elevators on the Plaza level and Level 1, with pay stations beside them.
quote: The Fountain Square North Garage, located directly beneath the Square, features 600 spaces spread across four underground levels.
Pay stations are located next to the elevators on the Plaza level and Level 1 of the Garage.

facts.claim: Public restrooms are on the west ramp leading up from Vine Street toward the garage entrance, open 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. but closing at 4 p.m. when no evening event is scheduled. Their accessibility is not stated. Movable umbrellas provide shade on the plaza.
quote: Public restrooms are located on the west ramp leading up from Vine Street toward the parking garage portal.
They are open to the public from 6am to 11pm every day. In the instance that no evening event is programmed on the Square, restrooms will close at 4pm.
28 umbrellas – compliments of Strauss Troy – keep the plaza cool and comfortable when the sun is overhead. The umbrellas are mobile so you can put them right where you want them!

facts.claim: For medically necessary equipment charging, ask at the Fountain Square concession stand. The rules say outlets may be available in some circumstances, primarily during events, and staff will try to accommodate requests; a power source is not guaranteed.
quote: In certain circumstances, primarily when events are actively taking place, the electrical outlets in certain locations in Fountain Square can be made available to park patrons for medically necessary devices.
If you must charge your medically necessary equipment, 3CDC staff members will work to accommodate you to the best of our ability during your visit to Fountain Square.
To access a power source for your medically necessary equipment, visit the Fountain Square Concession Stand and ask as staff member for proper accommodations.

facts.claim: The square is closed from 3 a.m. to 6 a.m. except for reaching the garage or nearby buildings. Downtown Ambassadors answer questions and give directions at (513) 623-3429.
quote: Fountain Square is closed from 3:00 AM to 6:00 AM except for the purpose of entering and exiting the garage or adjacent buildings.
Call the Ambassador Hotline at (513) 623-3429 if you have questions or concerns, need directions or a map to a Downtown destination.

facts.claim: Restroom attendants are on duty during larger events; if the restrooms are closed during posted hours, Ambassadors can explain why or open them when possible.
quote: Restroom Attendants are also on duty inside the bathrooms during larger events.
Should one find the restroom closed during the hours it should be open, available Ambassadors would be happy to explain why, or open it up when possible.

facts.claim: If no event is taking place or the concession stand is closed, seek a 3CDC operations staff member about charging medically necessary equipment. Staff will try to accommodate the request.
quote: Note that if no events are taking place during your visit and/or the Fountain Square Concession Stand is closed, you should seek out a 3CDC operations staff member, and staff will try to accommodate your request.

facts.claim: Winterhaus permits outside food and non-alcoholic drinks if at least one person in the group buys an item there. Its rules request a 30-minute seated limit for individuals who do not buy anything, and a one-hour seat limit for all guests.
quote: Patrons are welcome to bring outside food and non-alcoholic beverages, but at least one member of any group utilizing the space must purchase at least one item from Winterhaus.
Individuals who do not purchase an item from the Winterhaus are respectfully asked to limit their time in seated spaces to no more than 30 minutes to accommodate other patrons.
To ensure this space is accessible and enjoyable for all intended guests, please limit use of seats provided to 1-hour.

facts.claim: Fountain Square North Garage vehicle ramps enter from northbound Vine Street between Fifth and Sixth Streets and southbound Walnut Street between Sixth and Fifth. This is the garage beneath the square; Fountain Square South is a different garage.
quote: The Fountain Square North Garage, located directly beneath the Square, features 600 spaces spread across four underground levels.
the garage's two entrance/exit ramps are located on northbound Vine Street between Fifth & Sixth Streets, and on southbound Walnut Street between Sixth & Fifth Streets.
There are other garages near Fountain Square with similar names, including the Fountain Square South Garage, which 3CDC does not manage.

facts.claim: Take the garage ticket with you and pay at a pay station before returning to your car. Stations beside the elevators on Plaza level and Level 1 accept cash or credit card; feed the paid ticket into the exit machine.
quote: Take your ticket with you!
As you walk back to your car, stop at one of the pay station machines to pay your parking fee using cash or credit card.
Pay stations are located next to the elevators on the Plaza level and Level 1 of the Garage.
As you drive out, simply feed your paid ticket into the machine, and the arm will raise.

facts.claim: Winterhaus requires adults to show ID at the entrance; minors must be accompanied by an adult.
quote: Minors unaccompanied by an adult are not permitted. Adults are required to show ID at the entrance.

facts.claim: The Winterhaus page describes a heated, glass-enclosed tent and advertises a November–March season. Confirm operating hours before relying on it as a warm rest stop.
quote: Open from November - March, Winterhaus is a hub for festive fun!
Winterhaus is a heated, glass-enclosed, 65ft x 65ft tented retreat in the heart of Downtown Cincinnati.
Full and partial space rental opportunities are available for holiday parties, corporate events, birthdays and more.

facts.claim: The lodge lists an accessible front entrance, designated accessible parking on site, and accessible common-area restrooms and water fountains.
quote: Accessible front entrance
Onsite designated accessible parking
Accessible common area restrooms and water fountains

facts.claim: The accessibility page lists pool areas with some combination of sloped zero-depth entries, transport systems or pool lifts, plus a limited number of free waterproof wheelchairs at specific locations. It does not identify the equipment at each Mason pool.
quote: Pool areas with some combination of sloped zero-depth entries, transport systems or pool lifts for accessibility
A limited number of waterproof wheelchairs are available for use at no charge at specific locations

facts.claim: Wheelchairs can be borrowed temporarily from Guest Services, first come, first served.
quote: Temporary use of wheelchairs are available through Guest Services on a first come, first serve basis.

facts.claim: Closed captioning or transcripts are available for certain attractions with audio, including MagiQuest, and equipment to help with hearing is available on request.
quote: Closed captioning and/or transcripts available for certain attractions featuring audible entertainment, including our interactive live-action game MagiQuest
Equipment available upon request to assist with audibility needs

facts.claim: A downloadable sensory guide, developed with IBCCES, covers each slide, pool, ride, attraction, show and activity.
quote: As part of this partnership, IBCCES helped us develop a sensory guide for each slide, pool, ride, attraction, show and activity found at Great Wolf Lodge.
We hope this downloadable guide provides a valuable and convenient tool for sensory-sensitive guests as they plan their visit to our resort.

facts.claim: Accessible pathways run from the front desk to guest rooms, with accessible elevators and common-area corridors at least 36 inches wide.
quote: Accessible pathways from front desk to guestrooms, including accessible elevators to other floors of the hotel and common area corridors of 36” width or wider

facts.claim: In its FAQ answer about scooters, Segways and hoverboards, Great Wolf asks guests operating a mobility device for medical purposes to provide medical documentation on arrival. Confirm how the lodge applies this published request to your device before travelling.
quote: Can I use drones, scooters, Segways or Hoverboards inside the lodge?
If you operate a mobility device for medical purposes please provide medical documentation upon arrival.

facts.claim: The FAQ permits service animals except in water-park pools and attractions. Outside food and drink are generally excluded from the water park; personalized desserts may be approved in advance if made in a licensed, nut-free facility with a purchase receipt. Allergen-free alternatives can be discussed ahead of time. Pool chairs are first come, first served.
quote: Service animals as defined by the ADA are allowed in all areas of the resort. For the health and safety of our guests, service animals are not allowed in the pools and attractions of the water park.
There is no outside food or drink allowed in the water park, including glass containers and personal coolers.

Birthday cakes, cupcakes, or other personalized desserts may be allowed in the water park with prior approval from the lodge. They must be prepared in a licensed, nut-free facility and accompanied by a purchase receipt.
We would be happy to discuss allergen-free alternatives in advance.
Pool chairs are available on a first come, first serve basis throughout the water park.

facts.claim: The Mason FAQ says waterslides and elevated attractions are not wheelchair accessible.
quote: Waterslides and our elevated attractions are not wheelchair accessible.

facts.claim: Accessible suites are marked with an accessibility icon during booking. The FAQ lists 800-605-9653 for guests who prefer to reserve by phone.
quote: Accessible suites are labeled as such and marked by an accessible icon within the booking process. If you would prefer to make a reservation over the phone, please call 800.605.9653.

facts.claim: The water park has showers, changing areas and lockers. The FAQ does not describe transfer space, accessible changing benches or adult changing tables.
quote: There are lockers, showers, and changing areas available for your use in the water park.

facts.claim: Electronic lockers in the locker-room area can be rented for a fee in standard, large and jumbo sizes. The FAQ asks guests to keep anything larger than a standard suitcase in their room or vehicle.
quote: There are electronic lockers available to rent for a nominal fee in our locker room area. They come in a choice of three sizes: Standard, large and jumbo. Any items or luggage larger than a standard size suitcase should be kept in your room or vehicle.

facts.claim: The lodge posts quiet hours from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.; this is a policy, not a guarantee of a quiet room or environment.
quote: 11:00 p.m. -7:00 a.m. are the quiet hours for the lodge.

facts.claim: For dietary planning, the FAQ asks guests to contact the lodge and speak with a Food and Beverage Management team member about their needs and dining options.
quote: By providing us with information about your needs the Culinary Department can assist with your dining options.
Please contact the lodge to speak with a Food and Beverage Management team member.

facts.claim: The accessibility page permits service animals except in or near pools. Confirm permitted waiting and circulation areas with the lodge.
quote: Specifically, our facilities permit service animals (other than in or near pools)

facts.claim: CAIN says the lobby is reached only by stairs and asks visitors who need to avoid them to tell staff on arrival so they can take them around to the pantry. It describes the pantry as usable with a mobility aid; the alternate door and route dimensions are not specified.
quote: The lobby is only accessible by stairs, however the pantry is completely accessible by mobility aid device. Let us know upon arrival if you need to skip the stairs and we will take you around.

facts.claim: The Market page says there are restrooms usable with a mobility aid. It does not describe their layout, transfer space or changing equipment.
quote: There are restrooms that are accessible by mobility aid device as well.

facts.claim: The Market serves all ZIP codes and does not ask visitors to bring documents. Guests are asked to fill out information about themselves and their household.
quote: We serve ALL zip codes !
You do not need to bring any documentation when you visit. We will ask you to fill out some information about yourself and anyone you consider a part of your household.

facts.claim: On Mondays, sign-in opens at 4:30 p.m. and shopping runs 5–7 p.m. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, sign-in opens at 9:30 a.m. and shopping runs 10 a.m.–1 p.m. The line closes at capacity or 15 minutes before the Market closes.
quote: Mondays: line opens at 4:30 pm, Market opens from 5 pm – 7 pm
Tuesdays and Thursdays: line opens at 9:30 am, Market opens from 10 am – 1 pm
The line closes when we’ve reached capacity or 15 minutes before the Market closes.

facts.claim: Guests can join the line by text, website, app or in person once sign-in opens. For text sign-in, send one first name and one last name to 513-548-1024; only one person can be signed up per text.
quote: When the line opens, guests can sign in using text, online, an app or in person.
You can not sign in any earlier than the times posted above.
Text your name to 513-548-1024.
The system will only take up to one first and one last name.
You can only sign up one person at a time via text.

facts.claim: Staff can sign guests in person if they have no phone or other device. CAIN recommends arriving about 10 minutes before sign-in opens; the separate capacity cutoff still applies.
quote: If you do not have access to a cell phone or other device we are happy to sign you in in-person!
We recommend you arrive about 10 minutes before the line opens if you would like to ensure your place in line that day.
The line closes when we’ve reached capacity or 15 minutes before the Market closes.

facts.claim: The online sign-in page lets guests choose a language, but CAIN warns that closing the page prevents checking your place in line. App users can find CAIN in WaitWell after setting up their name and phone number.
quote: Find our page here , choose your language, and complete the form. Be aware if you close the page you will not be able to check on your place in line.
Find the ‘WaitWell’ app in your device’s app store, set up your name and phone number, and find us by searching ‘CAIN’.

facts.claim: A neighbor, family member, friend or client who cannot attend may have someone shop for them. The Market lets shoppers choose items from the shelves; CAIN recommends knowing the other person’s preferences before visiting.
quote: You are welcome to shop for a neighbor, family member, friend or client if they cannot make it to the market themselves.

We are a CHOICE pantry – which means you will be able to pick out items as you would in a grocery store. If you are shopping for someone else, it is helpful to know what their preferences are before coming to make shopping quick and easy.

facts.claim: Bring bags for groceries. CAIN can provide boxes and donated bags when available; carrying or loading assistance is not specified.
quote: Please bring your own bags. We can provide boxes and donated bags as they are available.

facts.claim: At the adjacent Annette’s House, CAIN identifies a ramp at the back. This is a separate building from the Market; its page does not establish the parking-to-ramp route, door controls or ramp dimensions.
quote: Annette’s House is accessible with a ramp in the back
purchasing the house next door to its main Northside building.

facts.claim: CAIN lists two single-use bathrooms at Annette’s House and describes one as ADA compliant. This is the publisher’s description; no measurements or adult changing equipment are given.
quote: there are 2 single-use bathrooms, one of which is ADA compliant.

facts.claim: The Free Fridge is on the south side of Annette’s House at 4234 Hamilton Avenue. CAIN describes 24-hour access to donated food, with a refrigerator/freezer, microwave, hot and cold water tap and small pantry; this does not guarantee stock or an accessible route.
quote: The Free Fridge offers 24/7 access to free food donated by the community to be access at any time of need.
The fridge can be found on the southern side of Annette’s House (4234 Hamilton Ave), eqipped with a combination refrigerator/freezer, microwave, hot and cold water tap, and a small pantry.

facts.claim: CAIN’s Monday community meal starts at 3:30 p.m., with sit-down and takeaway options. Meals are limited in quantity and first come, first served; no paperwork, documents or registration are needed.
quote: Every Monday at 3:30 pm , CAIN volunteers serve a meal with the option to either sit down to eat and watch a movie, play games, or enjoy the camaraderie, or take the meal to-go.
Meals are first-come first-served, and limited in quantity. No paperwork, documents or registration needed - just show up!

facts.claim: The Thursday Peace Potluck runs 6–8 p.m., either inside Annette’s House at 4234 Hamilton Avenue or in its front parking lot. CAIN describes the space as wheelchair accessible, but gives no route measurements or entrance details; confirm which location is being used.
quote: Third Way Peace Fellowship offers a free community meal every Thursday from 6:00 pm - 8:00 pm , either inside of Annette's House (4234 Hamilton Ave) or in the front parking lot. The space is wheelchair accessible.

facts.claim: During pantry hours, people experiencing homelessness may request a snack pack. CAIN describes these as quick-meal bags that usually contain shelf-stable, no-cook, individually sized items; contents vary.
quote: During pantry, anyone experiencing homelessness may request a 'snack pack'.
A snack pack is a bag of food meant to provide a quick breakfast or lunch plus a little extra until their next meal.
They usually include shelf-stable, no-cook, individually-sized items like chips, cookies, a sandwich, drinks and more.
